text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
German aircraft designer, WILLY MESSERSCHMITT, was born in 1898. He was best known for his World War Two planes, notably the Me-109 fighter and the twin-engined pioneering jet fighter, the Me-262.
PETER LORRE, Hungarian actor notably in "M", "The Maltese Falcon", "Casablanca" and "Arsenic and Old Lace", was born as Lazlo Loewenstein in 1904.
Australian opera singer JUNE BRONHILL (JUNE GOUGH) was born in 1929 in Broken Hill.
British singer and pianist, GEORGIE FAME (CLIVE POWELL) was born in 1943.
British guitarist MICK JONES, who formed the 'Clash' in 1976 with JOE STRUMMER, was born in 1955.
American singer and songwriter with 'Berlin', TERRI NUNN, was born in 1961. Best known hit was "Take My Breath Away", the love theme from the film "Top Gun".
** EVENTS **
1284 : The Pied Piper lured 130 children of Hamelin away
and they were never seen again. Although the fact is true, the reasons behind it are obscured by legend and the story that he did it in revenge for not being paid for clearing the town of
rats was a fiction added later.
1483 : RICHARD III of England began his rule, after
deposing his nephew EDWARD V. EDWARD and his brother RICHARD were later murdered.
1541 : FRANCISCO PIZARRO, Spanish conqueror of Peru, was
assassinated in his palace in Lima.
1830 : GEORGE IV of Great Britain died. He had been king
since 1820 and regent since 1811 when his father GEORGE III became insane.
1843 : Hong Kong was proclaimed a British Crown Colony
with Sir HENRY POTTINGER as its first governor.
1857 : The new military honour, the VICTORIA CROSS, was
awarded for the first time. Queen VICTORIA presented the medals to 62 servicemen at a ceremony in Hyde Park.
1858 : The Treaty of Tientsin was signed, ending
hostilities between China and Great Britain and granting the latter trade rights.
1906 : The first Grand Prix was run at Le Mans.
1930: Soviet leader, JOSEPH STALIN, announced his purges
were "purifying" the country.
1945 : The United Nations Charter was signed by 50
nations in San Francisco, succeeding the League of Nations. It became effective on October 24.
1950 : The United States entered the Korean War.
President HARRY S. TRUMAN ordered American forces to go to the aid of South Korea in its fight to repell the invaders from the north.
1959 : The St Lawrence Seaway, connecting the Great Lakes
with the Atlantic, was opened by Queen ELIZABETH II and President EISENHOWER.
1963 : During a tour of West Germany, President KENNEDY
told a crowd: "Ich bin ein Berliner".
1975 : More than 500 political opponents of Indian Prime
Minister INDIRA GANDHI were arrested and emergency regulations were brought into force.
1976 : London had a record temperature of 95 degrees F,
35 degrees C.
1977 : ELVIS PRESLEY made his final concert performance
at Indianapolis; he died two months later.
1978 : Australia approved the sale of 10,000 tonnes of
uranium to Britain.
1979 : United States boxer, MUHAMMAD ALI, announced his
retirement.
1984 : FIDEL CASTRO freed 22 jailed Americans after talks
with the Reverend JESSE JACKSON.
1990 : The IRA bombed London's Carlton club, a popular
meeting place for conservative members of the British parliament.
1991 : After a legal battle of 15 years the Maguire Seven
were cleared of running an IRA bomb factory. Their convictions were quashed after all seven had served their full sentences.
1995 : Egyptian President HOSNI MUBARAK survived an
assassination attempt.
